internal.title: Incident Report: Checkout Service High Error Rate Due to Payment Service Error Injection
internal.body:
On 2026-11-08 at 11:44 UTC, an alert was triggered for a high error rate in the checkout service. Initial diagnosis identified a high error rate and elevated latency in the payment service caused by an active error injection flag (paymentFailure). This flag was injecting errors into the payment service, resulting in a 50% error rate and increased latency, which cascaded to the checkout service causing a 47.5% error rate and elevated latency there as well.

The mitigation involved disabling the paymentFailure flag at 12:04 UTC after approval. Following this action, error rates and latencies in both payment and checkout services returned to normal levels, confirming recovery.

The frontend service also showed elevated errors but was not the primary cause.

Timeline:
- 11:44 UTC: Alert received for checkout service error rate spike
- 12:04 UTC: Diagnosis confirmed payment service error injection
- 12:04 UTC: PaymentFailure flag disabled after approval
- 12:04 UTC: Verified recovery with normalized error rates

Severity: SEV2

external.title: Some checkouts failed due to payment processing errors
external.body:
Between 11:44 and 12:04 UTC on 2026-11-08, some customers experienced issues completing checkout due to errors in the payment processing system. The issue was identified and resolved by disabling a fault injection mechanism affecting payment processing. Normal service was restored shortly after.

We apologize for any inconvenience caused and are reviewing our processes to prevent similar incidents in the future.
